full_judgment: "Para 5. But on perusual of the judgment of the High Court Division it is found that learned Advocate of both the parties who appeared there were confused between the period of subsistence of a usufructuary mortgage and the period of limitation in the case of a suit for redemption of a mortgaged land. The maximum period for which a usufructuary mortgage can be entered into was fifteen years under section 95 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950, but by ordinance No. XXI of 1969 section 95 was amended and thereby the maximum period for usufructuary mortgage was reduced to seven years. And unless earlier redeemed by repayment of the consideration a mortgager acquires right to redemption on the expiry of the maximum period of seven yeas, and if the mortgage does not voluntarily restore possession of the land to the corgagor, the latter may file a suit for redemption within a period of 60  wars from the date of accrual of his right of redemption. In this case the suit of redemption and as such it is not barred by limitation."
